Palpation of the involved area revealed crepitus consistent with subcutaneous emphysema, and there was 2.5-mm relative proptosis by the Hertel exophthalmometry. There was no other evidence of infectious cellulitis: the involved area was not erythematous, warm, or tender.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 79-year-old man presented six days after zygomatic implant placement with acute-onset painless swelling of the left periorbital region and cheek. Physical examination revealed marked swelling with palpable crepitus consistent with subcutaneous emphysema, 2.5-mm relative proptosis, and absence of infectious signs (no erythema, warmth, or tenderness). CT imaging confirmed subcutaneous air extending into the left periocular area and orbit, with visualization of a defect in the left maxillary wall adjacent to the dental implant serving as the source of air tracking. Given the absence of clinical or radiographic infection, the patient was managed conservatively with close observation, and the subcutaneous emphysema and proptosis resolved spontaneously.
